pr_title: [Fix] Update fileitem stream details from the currently playing stream
pr_body: ## Description Fixes the issue where playing Iso's or DVD/Bluray structured directories no longer updates the fileitem details. ## Motivation and Context Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/18702 ## How Has This Been Tested? Tested against iso images and dvd structure directories. Before playing the test files the GUI only showed the length of the item. After playing, all flags were shown correctly. ## Screenshots (if appropriate): Before playing. After playing ## Types of change - [X] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] **Clean up** (non-breaking change which removes non-working, unmaintained functionality) - [ ] **Improvement** (non-breaking change which improves existing functionality) - [ ] **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] **Breaking change** (fix or feature that will cause existing functionality to change) - [ ] **Cosmetic change** (non-breaking change that doesn't touch code) - [ ] **None of the above** (please explain below) ## Checklist: - [X] My code follows the **[Code Guidelines](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/docs/CODE_GUIDELINES.md)** of this project - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation, either Doxygen or wiki - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly - [X] I have read the **[Contributing](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)** document - [ ] I have added tests to cover my change - [ ] All new and existing tests passed
pr_comments: The best approach to fix this is to purge out this IsBetterStream crap. Should be fairly easy for Bluray because it doesn't use the NAV source in selections streams anymore.

> I've looked at the audio codec stuff in more detail and the reason it is missing is that `CDVDInputStreamNavigator` doesn't return any audio codec info to store in the selectionstream. Current behaviour therefore is to not show any codec flags for dvd audio streams, just the number of channels. I'd prefer in that case to use the codecID from the hint to correctly show the flags. This would require an additional audiocodec PCM flag adding to skins, named `pcm_dvd.png`. Other formats (DD etc) will already display correctly.
> @jjd-uk is correct in that `CDVDInputStreamNavigator` could be altered to return `mpeg2` rather than `h262` which means no skin modifications would be necessary for the video codec.
> Instead of the if statement, audio codec info can be obtained with
> `info.codecName = !s.codec.empty()? s.codec : avcodec_get_name(m_CurrentAudio.hint.codec);` This keeps original behaviour as far as possible but returns `pcm_dvd` for lpcm dvd audio.
> @arnova @enen92 Is that acceptable to you guys? If so I'll go ahead and make the changes.

Sounds good to me. IMO mpeg2 as far more common/known than h262. So I don't understand why mpeg2 wasn't chosen there instead of h262. Are we sure changing it doesn't cause any other problems?

EDIT: Read the comment incorrectly
Thanks for updating it, lgtm now. Did you happen to check whether we get a proper ar for video and channel count for audio with this?

For DVD yes.  For bluray the AR is reported by the player while it's playing but is not in the streamdetails although everything else is.  Means it doesn't get stored in the db.  Don't yet know why that info is missing, there is a lot of code to try and understand.
Ha, aspect ratio wasn't being added to the selectionstream so it always defaulted to zero. Now corrected.

issue_context.title: StreamDetails broken for DVD, Bluray and ISO
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug

Sometime early 2019 a change to v18 caused a break in populating the **streamdetails** table. 

A few attempts were made to fix the issue, ultimately resulting in a change to the way streamdetails were read and saved.

This new method will only read and save streamdetails in the following instances:

1. First scan of the movie \ episode (not subsequent delete from library and rescan)
2. Refresh of the movie \ episode

It no longer saves streamdetails from playback.

This caused a flood of complaints, and we still receive complaints about missing streamdetails and missing flags

Some relevant PR's here...
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/12651
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/15589
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/15896
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/15929
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/16342





## Expected Behavior

Streamdetails for every type of video file/folder handled by Kodi should populate the streamdetails table.



## Actual Behavior
The current implemented method in v18 and v19 does not work for the following:

Movies or episodes saved with Bluray folder structure
Movies or episodes saved with DVD folder structure
Movies or episodes saved as an ISO file

Which means this works in a single instance only - when using single video files.

This does not work as expected for TV Shows even when using standard single video files like mkv. Refreshing the TV Show and then answering Yes to refresh the episodes does not refresh streamdetails.

Each episode needs to be refreshed individually for this to work. If there are 50 episodes in the show, that is a lot of work to refresh each episode.

Refreshing is not the way to go. It kills any personal edits the user has made for that movie/episode.

Could this entire approach be redesigned. It really is making a mess of peoples libraries.



## Possible Fix




### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.  Scan a bluray structure movie into the library.
2.  Note the missing codecs / flags.
3.


### Debuglog
The debuglog can be found here:



### Screenshots 
Here are some links or screenshots to help explain the problem:

Flags / codecs displayed for single file videos (mkv, avi, etc)
![singlefile](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44626605/97818458-a3c41000-1cf6-11eb-963a-6b3501916e49.jpg)


Bluray structure displays no flags / codecs
![bluray](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44626605/97818483-c6eebf80-1cf6-11eb-9746-00941e7edc9f.jpg)

Fair comment, I am trying to figure out exactly what is wrong.  From what I can see, SelectionStreams contains the following data for the video stream when playing my test iso. `source = 512`, `id = 1`, `demuxerId = -1`.  m_CurrentVideo contains `source = 256`, `id = 0`, `demuxerId = 3`.  So `m_SelectionStreams.TypeIndexOf()` is never going to find a match and the returned streamId is always -1
The older code obtained the stream id via `CDVDInputStreamNavigator()` for DVD's and used m_CurrentVideo/Audio for everything else.  My assumption from this is that m_CurrentVideo.id does not hold the correct stream id when playing dvd related content.  The older code also uses `STREAM_SOURCE_NAV` for the source id, rather than `m_CurrentVideo.source`. I presume this is for a similar reason, i.e. that the details held in `m_CurrentVideo/Audio` are not populated correctly when playing dvd related material.  Is that anywhere near being correct ? review_comments: This is missing the condition "&& m_pInputStream->IsStreamType(DVDSTREAM_TYPE_DVD)". Probably causing the reported crash.

I also once created a PR with the exact same fix but it was never merged because of comments by @FernetMenta . Please see https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/16239

EDIT: So I think it *could* be set but I think it needs to be conditional....

It already should be by the if statement in `CApplication.cpp`.  We're only updating stuff using vp that doesn't already have any details and even then, only if it's from DVD or Bluray. Everything else is updated by the background loader isn't it ? I've tested this by removing everything from the streamdetails table in the db then playing something not dvd related that the background loader hasn't got to yet and the details were not updated from vp.
Ok, then I guess we should be ok.
